  • As , , , , and are all involved in the initial plans for Metropolis Terminal, they are numbered lines 1-6.
  • and are large ring lines for West and East Los Sengas respectively, with the former being the first line to be established and complete construction, and the latter being the first line to exceed 80 km, as well as the current longest line in the entire Los Sengas Nazca Railway network.
  • and are north-south oriented and east-west oriented lines respectively. They respectively draw the boundaries between East and West Los Sengas, and North and South Los Sengas. However, due to geological constraints, they do not completely stick along the X/Z Axis.
  • and respectively forms a south-oriented and north-oriented parabola along and travels to the four diagonals from the center. Noticeably, leans to the north with a larger magnitude than to the south, especially at the East.
  • Therefore, as the first line that is not the Core Lines of Metropolis Terminal, is assigned the Number 7.
  • currently has two branch lines:
  • As the first branch line of , is also the first line in Nazca Railway to pave tracks only after all stations along the line completed consturction.
  • is the Auxiliary Branch Line of that connects with the Nazca Railway Headquarters.
  • is the only line in Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division that has its Main Line split in two, as well as the second line to feature such a configuration, with the first line being of the Terracept Division.
  • and are the only two lines with known plans or already have Express Services that run in a similar style with Veloducts.
  • currently possess the longest Interstation Distance at 13.02km between and .
  • currently has:
  • The only track session that is shared by three lines in Nazca Railway (Between and , shared with and )
  • The first line to have three termini.
  • currently has one branch line:
  • is the first planned branch line in Nazca Railway, but is not the first to be established. This line originally had plans to have a semi-circular route, with both ends of the line connecting with . However, subsequent planning has found out that the original routing would overlap severely with , and coupled with the fact that Xofa does not have direct rail services to Teraleros, is therefore repurposed to be a north-south oriented line.
  • is named after the fact that it serves the West Metropolis Archipelago, but ironically, it is the last line in Season 1 to enter the West Metropolis Archipelago. Moreover, this line also faced multiple difficulties and changes in its planning stages, and more details of these can be seen at the page of that line.
  • serves as the branch line of , and has become a final substitute service for Mayler Airport as did not serve that airport.
  • currently has two branch lines, with plans for a third one:
  • is the first branch line of and Nazca Railway's first Branch Line to copmlete construction. As it references Ma On Shan Line of the MTR, it was the first line in Nazca Railway to be built to Sub-Standard Railway Standards. However, the entire line has since been expanded to Standard Railway Standards. Currently, this line is still the longest branch line in Nazca Railway at 16.17km long, and still possess the shortest Interstation Distance at 560m between and .
  • is the second branch line of ;
  • is the third branch line of under planning. Once complete, will be the first Nazca Railway line with three independent Branch Lines.
  • and also takes references to Tuen Ma Line (then Ma On Shan Line and West Rail Line respectively):
  • pays tribute to Ma On Shan Line, whereas the section between and for takes references to the section along the Pat Heung Depot of West Rail Line.
  • Rumors of the two lines merging together also exists, but ultimately, it didn't happen. Instead, the two lines interchange at and .
  • already has plans to have a second Terminus at besides of the first one at . However, this is not realized until S3E13P2.
  • is the first Nazca Railway line to adopt right-hand traffic, and its 0 mD Sign is located at the large triangluar interchange at Peckern between , and stations. Therefore, the Up and Down Platform Numbers were initially reversed between and . However, subsequent Station Numbering has ignored this fact, and has instead opted with Centopia being the "Zero Station".
  • , , all serve the Nazca Railway Headquarters, and as a result, the latter two lines follow up from the number of , and are assigned the numbers 10-12.
  • As a result, the Line Numbers of , , , and are rearranged, with the most apparent example being the number of being rearranged from 11 at the planning stages during S1E19 to the current Number 15.
  • and originally planned to be established when the Nazca Railway Headquarters are built, but due to the premature development of Xofa, these two lines are established in early on in S3E6.
  • <!--is a Standard Railway Line that is planned to connect Metropolis Terminal with the Los Sengas International and Intergalactic Transport Hub (SITH);
  • Initially, this line -->, in its initial incarnation, only passed through Katadelphia and did not have stations in that district. However, eventually, and are inserted in that district, and as a result, this line became the first line to have stations inserted in the middle more than once.
  • initially had plans to connect between and . However, due to Jupiter development, this line goes to instead, and this has also indirectly caused to serve parts of the original planned line.
  • During its planning stages, was named '''Snoast Line''', and its original route is also slightly different from its current Route. Eventually, this line, and are respectively planned to traverse through East, West and Central Ingress Continent from the South to the North.
  • , , and , alongside and , are planned by Nazca Railway to form a ring network around Metropolis Terminal during later stages of Season 2. This guarantees that passengers commuting between various Districts and Interchanging do not have to rely too heavily on lines entering Downtown.
  • once had two separate sections, with the west section being defined as . This also became the only example of a Temporary Line in Nazca Railway.
  • and are sister lines that mainly serve the West Metropolis Archipelago Vicinity, with being the first line that only sets station within the West Metropolis Archipelago.
  • is an Independent Branch Line that is derived from the original Branch, and connects between and . Thus, it is defined as a "Bypass".
  • Due to changes in plans and geological constraints, became the first line to adopt an Oceanfloor Station Design instead of the originally planned .
  • <!--, -->, , and are several circular lines planned by Nazca Railway that succeeds , . Unlike and , both of which covers large areas of Los Sengas, these four<!--five--> circular lines have aims to either serve specific districts or act as "Pioneer Lines" into new areas.
  • As the third line to form a complete ring, mainly serves Cometsilk and north Prymea. While is a rare instance of a Ring Line having a "Terminus", that station can also be seen as a part of the ring as passengers can choose to remain in teh train and travel to other stations along the original direction.
  • , and are all District Lines serving Peckern North:
  • took two and a half years between the planning and constructing stages, and in the meantime, Tin Shek New Town has also undergone reconstruction.
  • and has plans to cross-interchange in Pekcern North multiple times, with known instances including the already existing and , as well as the under planning .
  • is a long-term route that will extend to the northwest from Peckern North.
  • , and , alongside , and , are all major routes within the Ingress Continent.
  • mainly runs between the northwest and the southeast of Central Ingress Continent to facilitate passenger flow, whereas and , alongside are the main east-west oriented lines within the Ingress Continent.
  • The latter three (, and ), form a north-south grid network alongside .
  • and are sister lines within the "Strategic Railway Plan" of Nazca Railway. These two lines are built to further secure the grid tightness and interchange convenience among the Nazca Railway network. Interestingly, besides of the Butterfly-like routing within Downtown, the general direction of development of these two lines are similar to that of and .
  • Since the establishment of and in S3E16 and S3E18 respectively, these two lines have seen more frequent development than other lines, and has simultaneously broke the record of the Second Longest Line which was held by , and are currently the second and third longest lines respectively behind .
  • , and are District Lines in TriPaw and the Twenty-Second Continent.
  • mainly deals with serving passengers bewteen TriPaw and the Twenty-Second Continent, as well as increasing railway coverage in the middle of the Twenty-Second Continent. Its original circuitous route within TriPaw has also since been broken into ;
  • provides eastbound railway connections from TriPaw to Oasis and Prymea;
  • is the branch line for the Twenty-Second Continent section , and is built to further cover the south of the Twenty-Second Continent. Its overall route and design is similar to that of the initial plans of .
  • was initially planned as an auxiliary route at the south of Jupiter, but is now planned as another east-west oriented line that runs to the south of ;
  • The section between and shares structure with The Great Liberty Bridge, and with an interstation distance of 10.18km,, it has overtaken the Section between and of as the longest non-Express Line Interstation Distance in Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division).
  • and are lines planned around , and has long-term plans to serve Union and Duotwirl.

Other Facts

  • is the only line that serves Centopia and does not use it as its "Zero Station".
  • has the two widest sets of Island Platforms at Circle Pit Station (53m) and Wooden Abyss Station (55m).
  • and has a "D-shaped" route between and within the Egress Continent. Katadelphia Railway also adopted a similar design.
  • Parts of shares tracks with (Formerly ), between and .
  • is currently the only railway line travelling out of Teraleros, and was also formerly the only railway line travelling out of Xofa.
  • Plans for Ingress Diamond Station serving and already existed in S1E19 from inside the Station Control Room of Ingress South Station, but that station did not come into fruition until S2E12 when is established.
  • was formerly the longest Branch Line in Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division) at 10.395km, but was overtaken by another Branch Line of , in S3E13P2 at 10.66km. However, since S3E14P1, has reclaimed the record.
  • has a shorter average interstation distance than other lines between Savanna Central Station and North Mountain Station, but the interstation distance has returned normal between North Mountain Station and Peacean Island Station.
  • used to have the longest Standard Railway Interstation Distance between Internal Sea East Station and Flask East Checkpoint, but is ultimately replaced by . The longest Interstation Distance for non-express Lines is also replaced by .
  • has three consecutive stations in Ingress, Internal Sea and Flask. Coincidentally, the three consecutive stations not only exist in different Districts, but also contains the word "East", with East Margin Station corresponding to Ingress, Internal Sea East Station corresponding to Internal Sea, and Flask East Checkpoint corresponding to Flask.
  • Parts of shares tracks with .
  • already appeared in the form of reserved platforms in S1E19, but did not appear until S2E12.
  • has a higher-pitched announcement voice than other lines, reflecting the same scenario with the South Island Line in the MTR during its early stages of operation.
  • is the second line to adopt a Bridge Core Design at Elevated Sections after .
  • adopts an Oceanfloor Tube Tunnel Design between Causeway Bay Station and Qoser Coast Station, and is the fourth Line to adopt this Tunnel Design after , and .
  • All Stations along uses Liquid Platform Screen Doors and Glass Floors.
  • has a semi-circular shape between Cansand Bay Station and Southern Heights Station.
  • Parts of the Elevated Section of also adopts the Bridge Core Design, and sections to the south of Bottom Woods Station also adopts an Oceanfloor Tube Tunnel Design.
  • While passes through , and , it does not interchange with any of these lines.

'''Station Types''' refers to the various types of stations built by Nazca Railway according to their geographical location.

Types

According to the building format of NR, stations can be categorized into 8 types.

Type I

'''Type I''' stations, also known as Elevated Stations, are stations in which the platforms are built at least one floor above ground level. Most Type I Stations have elevated tracks at either direction of the platform.

Style

Most Elevated Stations make use of island platforms, where the concourses are located directly below the platforms. In most cases, the Concourse is located on Ground Level, but there are also some examples in which the concourse is also elevated, such as and .

However, some concourses, due to Geological constraints, would adopt unconventional designs when the station structure passes over other structures like rivers and roads, such as:

  • Concourses being split into two or more structures (eg. )
  • Shrunk Concourses that are shorter than the Platform (eg. )
  • Platforms and Concourses being built in separate structures (eg. )

Platforms and tracks of such stations are built on the ground, and side platforms are usually used. The concourses of these stations can be in various locations, either above, on the side of, or below platforms, with exits connecting the concourse and the ground outside of the station. However, there are also stations, such as , that put the exit directly next to the platforms.

'''Type III''' stations are also known as Underground Stations, and they are commonly found in urban and mountainous areas.

Style

Both the platforms and the concourses of such stations are located underground, with both island platforms and side platforms being considered when designing. Usually, for such stations, concourses are located above the platforms, featuring multiple exits to the surface. Some exits can be extended by tunnels, and as a result, exits may not need to be located next to the main structure.

Type IV

'''Type IV''' stations are also known as Island Stations. It is named after the fact that the first time Nazca Railway adopts such a design is at the West Metropolis Archipelago. These stations are found in island areas if Type VII station is not considered, but with a minority of exceptions. This station type is also seen in areas with small underground space.

Style

This type of stations commonly uses split stacked platforms, with narrower platform widths. Such designs enable stations to be built with little underground space. Such an arrangement is common in island areas and areas with intensive urban development, such as Red Millet Station.

The councourse is mostly constructed on top of the upper platform, with exits that adopt a similar design of Type III Stations. Stations may even be connected to neighbouring light rails with flexibility depending on the negotiation between Nazca Railway and the local developers. As a result, "Octopus Exits", which refer to exits being located far from the concourse, is common in this type of stations.

As some islands have decentralized structures, some stations will also feature a passenger shuttle for exits, with being a prominent example.

'''Type V''' stations, also known as Pseudoground Stations, are derived from the Typ III Underground Stations.

Style

Despite being called Pseudo'''ground''' Stations, the structure of such stations resembles Underground Stations. However, unlike Underground Stations, the concourses of Pseudoground Stations are on ground level, while the platforms are designed in a fashion similar to Ground Stations. The most obvious difference is that Pseudoground Stations use Platform Gates while Underground Stations use Platform Screen Doors.

Style

The platforms are built on the oceanfloor, with glass covering the platform structure in a fashion similar to an aquarium. Depending on the size of the island and the surrounding terrain, the concourses can be built either are sea or under land.

As these stations may not need to built in the island itself, this design ensures that smaller islands and areas with limited usable underground space could be covered by NR. Sometimes, two islands can share one station. Currently, and are the only examples of Type VII Stations that are not built next to an island.

Also, a water pool 3 to 8 meters deep is created in each station in a fashion similar to a cave, hence the name of this station type.

'''Stem Island''' is one of the islands on West Metropolis Archipelago. It is also a constituent of the Note Group.

Location

Stem Island is located between Heeled Island and Caver Island. passes over the west of this island without stopping, and it is also the westernmost island among the Note Group. Tower Isle to the northwest of this island is a subsidiary isle of this island.
